comments.note: archiveDocuments() catches all errors in the copyFile call (not just ENOENT), so permission errors or disk-full conditions would silently be counted as 'skipped' rather than propagating. This is consistent with the best-effort design intent stated in the plan, but a future improvement could distinguish ENOENT (expected skip) from unexpected I/O errors (which might warrant a louder warning level).

summary: Reviewed project-lifecycle.ts: archiveDocuments() call placement is correct in both tools — inside withLock for completeSynthesis (line 410), after writeRootIndex/writeProjectMeta for initializeProject (line 304). No ordering or scope violations.
Reviewed Zod schema: CompleteSynthesisSchema synthesis_file is optional z.string().default('synthesis.md') — correct typing, correct default.

Reviewed response payload shape: archive_skipped uses length>0 ternary to omit the field when empty (rather than returning []). This is clean, consistent, and matches good API design — callers can distinguish 'no skips' from 'skip list present' without null checks.

Reviewed 7 new tests: happy path (copy succeeds + file readable), missing source (archive_skipped present, tool still succeeds), custom filename, and the critical 'plan NOT re-archived at synthesis' isolation test. Test coverage is comprehensive and the isolation test is particularly valuable.
No blocking issues found. Implementation is clean, well-placed, and consistent with existing patterns.

comments.note: simulateCompleteSynthesis and simulateInitializeProject inline helpers duplicate tool internals — this is the established codebase pattern (synthesis-terminal.test.ts does the same) and is acceptable. If these tools accumulate more complexity in future, exporting the bare implementation functions would be a cleaner testability boundary.

archiveDocuments() currently catches all errors (ENOENT and non-ENOENT) and counts all failures as 'skipped'. This aligns with the best-effort design intent, but if the storage directory fills up or has a permissions problem, the archival will silently no-op with a 'skipped' entry rather than surfacing an I/O warning. Low risk today; consider ENOENT discrimination for future hardening in the LedgerStore implementation.
